question.problem: Find the solutions of the equation $20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}=6p.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(p)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2} & =6p \\ 20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}-6p & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $p.$ We can factor out the $p$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}-6p & =0 \\ p(20{p}^{2}+7p-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $20{p}^{2}+7p-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(20{p}^{2}+7p-6) & =0 \\ p(5p-2)(4p+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p=0,$ $p=\frac{2}{5},$ and $p=-\frac{3}{4}.$
